## Supertrend

<a id="opIdGetTimeSeriesSuperTrend"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.twelvedata.com/supertrend?interval=1min' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /supertrend`

The Supertrend endpoint provides data on the Supertrend indicator, a tool used to identify potential buy and sell signals in trending markets. It returns values that indicate the current trend direction and potential reversal points based on price, time, and volatility. Users can leverage this data to pinpoint optimal entry and exit points for trades.

<h3 id="supertrend-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|symbol|query|string|false|Symbol ticker of the instrument. E.g. `AAPL`, `EUR/USD`, `ETH/BTC`, ...|
|isin|query|string|false|Filter by international securities identification number (ISIN). ISIN access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|figi|query|string|false|The FIGI of an instrument for which data is requested. This parameter is available on the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing">Ultra</a> plan (individual) and the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing-business">Enterprise</a> plan (business) and above.|
|cusip|query|string|false|The CUSIP of an instrument for which data is requested. CUSIP access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|interval|query|[IntervalEnum](#schemaintervalenum)|true|Interval between two consecutive points in time series|
|outputsize|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of data points to retrieve. Supports values in the range from `1` to `5000`. Default `30` when no date parameters are set, otherwise set to maximum|
|exchange|query|string|false|Exchange where instrument is traded|
|mic_code|query|string|false|Market Identifier Code (MIC) under ISO 10383 standard|
|country|query|string|false|The country where the instrument is traded, e.g., `United States` or `US`|
|type|query|[TypeEnum](#schematypeenum)|false|The asset class to which the instrument belongs|
|timezone|query|string|false|Timezone at which output datetime will be displayed. Supports:<br><ul><br><li>1. <code>Exchange</code> for local exchange time</li><br><li>2. <code>UTC</code> for datetime at universal UTC standard</li><br><li>3. Timezone name according to the IANA Time Zone Database. E.g. <code>America/New_York</code>, <code>Asia/Singapore</code>. Full list of timezones can be found <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tz_database_time_zones" target="blank">here</a></li><br></ul><br><p>Interval Limitation: The timezone parameter is only applicable for intraday intervals (less than 1 day). For intervals of 1day, 1week, or 1month, the timezone parameter is ignored, and data is strictly returned in the Exchange local time.</p><br><i>Take note that the IANA Timezone name is case-sensitive</i>|
|start_date|query|string|false|Can be used separately and together with `end_date`. |end_date|query|string|false|The ending date and time for data selection, see `start_date` description for details.|

|order|query|[OrderEnum](#schemaorderenum)|false|Sorting order of the output|
|prepost|query|boolean|false|Returns quotes that include pre-market and post-market data. Only for the `Pro` plan (individual) and `Venture` plan (business) and above.<br>Available at the `1min`, `5min`, `15min`, and `30min` intervals for US equities.<br>Open, high, low, close values are supplied without volume|
|format|query|[FormatEnum](#schemaformatenum)|false|The format of the response data|
|delimiter|query|string|false|The separator used in the CSV response data|
|dp|query|integer(int64)|false|Specifies the number of decimal places for floating values.<br>Should be in range [0, 11] inclusive.<br>By default, the number of decimal places is automatically determined based on the values provided|
|previous_close|query|boolean|false|A boolean parameter to include the previous closing price in the time_series data. If true, adds previous bar close price value to the current object|
|adjust|query|[AdjustEnum](#schemaadjustenum)|false|Adjusting mode for prices|
|period|query|integer(int64)|false|The period used for calculation in the indicator. Takes values in the range from `1` to `800`|
|multiplier|query|integer(int64)|false|The factor used to adjust the indicator's sensitivity.|

## Triple exponential moving average

`GET /t3ma`

The Triple Exponential Moving Average (T3MA) endpoint calculates a smoothed moving average using three exponential moving averages on price data. It returns a dataset that highlights price trends with reduced lag, offering precise trend analysis. This is useful for identifying trend direction and potential reversal points.

## Triple exponential moving average

<a id="opIdGetTimeSeriesTema"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.twelvedata.com/tema?interval=1min' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /tema`

The Triple Exponential Moving Average (TEMA) endpoint calculates and returns the TEMA values for a specified financial instrument over a given time period. This endpoint provides a series of data points that smooth out price fluctuations by applying three layers of exponential moving averages, allowing users to identify and track underlying trends in the instrument's price movement.

## True range

<a id="opIdGetTimeSeriesTRange"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.twelvedata.com/trange?interval=1min' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /trange`

The True Range (TRANGE) endpoint calculates the range of price movement for a specified period, providing a measure of market volatility. It returns data that includes the highest and lowest prices over the period, along with the closing price from the previous period. This information is useful for traders to assess market volatility and adjust their trading strategies accordingly.

## Triangular moving average

<a id="opIdGetTimeSeriesTrima"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.twelvedata.com/trima?interval=1min' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /trima`

The Triangular Moving Average (TRIMA) endpoint calculates and returns the smoothed average price of a financial security over a specified period, with a focus on central data points. This endpoint provides a balanced view of price trends by applying a double smoothing process, making it useful for identifying underlying price patterns and reducing short-term fluctuations.

<h3 id="triangular-moving-average-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|symbol|query|string|false|Symbol ticker of the instrument. E.g. `AAPL`, `EUR/USD`, `ETH/BTC`, ...|
|isin|query|string|false|Filter by international securities identification number (ISIN). ISIN access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|figi|query|string|false|The FIGI of an instrument for which data is requested. This parameter is available on the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing">Ultra</a> plan (individual) and the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing-business">Enterprise</a> plan (business) and above.|
|cusip|query|string|false|The CUSIP of an instrument for which data is requested. CUSIP access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|

|outputsize|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of data points to retrieve. Supports values in the range from `1` to `5000`. Default `30` when no date parameters are set, otherwise set to maximum|
|exchange|query|string|false|Exchange where instrument is traded|
|mic_code|query|string|false|Market Identifier Code (MIC) under ISO 10383 standard|
|country|query|string|false|The country where the instrument is traded, e.g., `United States` or `US`|
|type|query|[TypeEnum](#schematypeenum)|false|The asset class to which the instrument belongs|
|timezone|query|string|false|Timezone at which output datetime will be displayed. Timezone name according to the IANA Time Zone Database. E.g. <code>America/New_York</code>, <code>Asia/Singapore</code>. Full list of timezones can be found <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tz_database_time_zones" target="blank">here</a></li><br></ul><br><p>Interval Limitation: The timezone parameter is only applicable for intraday intervals (less than 1 day). For intervals of 1day, 1week, or 1month, the timezone parameter is ignored, and data is strictly returned in the Exchange local time.</p><br><i>Take note that the IANA Timezone name is case-sensitive</i>|

|prepost|query|boolean|false|Returns quotes that include pre-market and post-market data. ## Time series forecast

`GET /tsf`

The Time Series Forecast (TSF) endpoint provides projected future price levels using linear regression analysis. It returns data that helps users identify potential support and resistance levels, as well as trend direction in a financial market. This endpoint is useful for traders seeking to anticipate price movements and adjust their strategies accordingly.

## Ultimate oscillator endpoint

<a id="opIdGetTimeSeriesUltOsc"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.twelvedata.com/ultosc?interval=1min' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /ultosc`

The Ultimate Oscillator endpoint (/ultosc) calculates a momentum oscillator that integrates short, intermediate, and long-term price movements to detect potential overbought or oversold conditions and possible trend reversals. It returns a time series of oscillator values, which can be used to assess market momentum and identify entry or exit points in trading strategies.

## Variance

<a id="opIdGetTimeSeriesVar"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.twelvedata.com/var?interval=1min' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /var`

The Variance (VAR) endpoint calculates the statistical variance of a financial data series, providing a measure of how much the data points deviate from the average value. It returns a numerical value representing this dispersion, which can be used to assess the volatility of a security over a specified period. This information is crucial for traders and analysts who need to evaluate the risk associated with price fluctuations in the market.

## Volume weighted average price

<a id="opIdGetTimeSeriesVwap"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.twelvedata.com/vwap?interval=1min' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /vwap`

The Volume Weighted Average Price (VWAP) endpoint provides the VWAP value for a specified stock or asset over a given time period. This indicator calculates the average price at which a security has traded throughout the day, based on both volume and price. It is useful for identifying the true average price of an asset, helping traders to assess the current price relative to the day's average.

<h3 id="volume-weighted-average-price-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|symbol|query|string|false|Symbol ticker of the instrument. E.g. `AAPL`, `EUR/USD`, `ETH/BTC`, ...|
|isin|query|string|false|Filter by international securities identification number (ISIN). ISIN access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|figi|query|string|false|The FIGI of an instrument for which data is requested. This parameter is available on the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing">Ultra</a> plan (individual) and the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing-business">Enterprise</a> plan (business) and above.|
|cusip|query|string|false|The CUSIP of an instrument for which data is requested. CUSIP access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|interval|query|[IntervalEnum](#schemaintervalenum)|true|Interval between two consecutive points in time series|
|outputsize|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of data points to retrieve. Supports values in the range from `1` to `5000`. Default `30` when no date parameters are set, otherwise set to maximum|

For intervals of 1day, 1week, or 1month, the timezone parameter is ignored, and data is strictly returned in the Exchange local time.</p><br><i>Take note that the IANA Timezone name is case-sensitive</i>|

## Weighted close price

<a id="opIdGetTimeSeriesWclPrice"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.twelvedata.com/wclprice?interval=1min' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /wclprice`

The Weighted Close Price (WCLPRICE) endpoint calculates a security's average price by giving additional weight to the closing price, using the formula: (High + Low + Close * 2) / 4.

## Williams %R

<a id="opIdGetTimeSeriesWillR"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.twelvedata.com/willr?interval=1min' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /willr`

The Williams %R (WILLR) endpoint calculates the Williams Percent Range, a momentum indicator that evaluates a security's closing price relative to its high-low range over a specified period. This endpoint returns data that helps users identify potential overbought or oversold conditions and possible trend reversals in the market.

## Weighted moving average

<a id="opIdGetTimeSeriesWma"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.twelvedata.com/wma?interval=1min' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /wma`

The Weighted Moving Average (WMA) endpoint calculates and returns the WMA values for a given security over a specified period. This endpoint provides a time series of weighted averages, where recent prices have a higher influence, allowing users to track and analyze short-term price trends effectively.

<h3 id="weighted-moving-average-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|symbol|query|string|false|Symbol ticker of the instrument. E.g. `AAPL`, `EUR/USD`, `ETH/BTC`, ...|
|isin|query|string|false|Filter by international securities identification number (ISIN). ISIN access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|figi|query|string|false|The FIGI of an instrument for which data is requested. This parameter is available on the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing">Ultra</a> plan (individual) and the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing-business">Enterprise</a> plan (business) and above.|
|cusip|query|string|false|The CUSIP of an instrument for which data is requested. CUSIP access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|interval|query|[IntervalEnum](#schemaintervalenum)|true|Interval between two consecutive points in time series|
|outputsize|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of data points to retrieve. Supports values in the range from `1` to `5000`. Default `30` when no date parameters are set, otherwise set to maximum|
|exchange|query|string|false|Exchange where instrument is traded|
|mic_code|query|string|false|Market Identifier Code (MIC) under ISO 10383 standard|
|country|query|string|false|The country where the instrument is traded, e.g., `United States` or `US`|
|type|query|[TypeEnum](#schematypeenum)|false|The asset class to which the instrument belongs|
|timezone|query|string|false|Timezone at which output datetime will be displayed. Supports:<br><ul><br><li>1. <code>Exchange</code> for local exchange time</li><br><li>2. <code>UTC</code> for datetime at universal UTC standard</li><br><li>3. Timezone name according to the IANA Time Zone Database. E.g. <code>America/New_York</code>, <code>Asia/Singapore</code>. Full list of timezones can be found <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tz_database_time_zones" target="blank">here</a></li><br></ul><br><p>Interval Limitation: The timezone parameter is only applicable for intraday intervals (less than 1 day). For intervals of 1day, 1week, or 1month, the timezone parameter is ignored, and data is strictly returned in the Exchange local time.</p><br><i>Take note that the IANA Timezone name is case-sensitive</i>|
|start_date|query|string|false|Can be used separately and together with `end_date`. Format `2006-01-02` or `2006-01-02T15:04:05`<br><br>Default location:<br><ul><br><li>Forex and Cryptocurrencies - <code>UTC</code></li><br><li>Stocks - where exchange is located (e.g. for AAPL it will be <code>America/New_York</code>)</li><br></ul><br>Both parameters take into account if <code>timezone</code> parameter is provided.<br/><br>If <code>timezone</code> is given then, <code>start_date</code> and <code>end_date</code> will be used in the specified location<br><br>Examples:<br><ul><br><li>1. <code>&symbol=AAPL&start_date=2019-08-09T15:50:00&…</code><br/><br>Returns all records starting from 2019-08-09T15:50:00 New York time up to current date</li><br><li>2. <code>&symbol=EUR/USD&timezone=Asia/Singapore&start_date=2019-08-09T15:50:00&…</code><br/><br>Returns all records starting from 2019-08-09T15:50:00 Singapore time up to current date</li><br><li>3. <code>&symbol=ETH/BTC&timezone=Europe/Zurich&start_date=2019-08-09T15:50:00&end_date=2019-08-09T15:55:00&...</code><br/><br>Returns all records starting from 2019-08-09T15:50:00 Zurich time up to 2019-08-09T15:55:00</li><br></ul>|
|end_date|query|string|false|The ending date and time for data selection, see `start_date` description for details.|
|date|query|string|false|Specifies the exact date to get the data for. Could be the exact date, e.g. `2021-10-27`, or in human language `today` or `yesterday`|
|order|query|[OrderEnum](#schemaorderenum)|false|Sorting order of the output|
|prepost|query|boolean|false|Returns quotes that include pre-market and post-market data. Only for the `Pro` plan (individual) and `Venture` plan (business) and above.<br>Available at the `1min`, `5min`, `15min`, and `30min` intervals for US equities.<br>Open, high, low, close values are supplied without volume|
|format|query|[FormatEnum](#schemaformatenum)|false|The format of the response data|
|delimiter|query|string|false|The separator used in the CSV response data|
|dp|query|integer(int64)|false|Specifies the number of decimal places for floating values.<br>Should be in range [0, 11] inclusive.<br>By default, the number of decimal places is automatically determined based on the values provided|

## Earnings estimate

<a id="opIdGetEarningsEstimate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.twelvedata.com/earnings_estimate \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /earnings_estimate`

The earnings estimate endpoint provides access to analysts' projected earnings per share (EPS) for a specific company, covering both upcoming quarterly and annual periods. This data is crucial for users who need to track and compare expected financial performance across different timeframes, aiding in the evaluation of a company's future profitability.

<h3 id="earnings-estimate-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|symbol|query|string|false|Filter by symbol|

## Revenue estimate

<a id="opIdGetRevenueEstimate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.twelvedata.com/revenue_estimate \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /revenue_estimate`

The revenue estimate endpoint provides a company's projected quarterly and annual revenue figures based on analysts' estimates. This data is useful for users seeking insights into expected company performance, allowing them to compare forecasted sales with historical data or other companies' estimates.

<h3 id="revenue-estimate-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|isin|query|string|false|Filter by international securities identification number (ISIN). ISIN access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|cusip|query|string|false|The CUSIP of an instrument for which data is requested. CUSIP access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|country|query|string|false|Filter by country name or alpha code, e.g., `United States` or `US`|
|exchange|query|string|false|Filter by exchange name|
|mic_code|query|string|false|The Market Identifier Code (MIC) of the exchange where the instrument is traded, e.g., XNAS, XLON.|
|dp|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of decimal places for floating values.<br>Should be in range [0,11] inclusive|

## Batches

<a id="opIdadvanced"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.twelvedata.com/batch \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "property1": {
      "url": "/time_series?symbol=AAPL&interval=1min&apikey=demo&outputsize=2"
    },
    "property2": {
      "url": "/time_series?symbol=AAPL&interval=1min&apikey=demo&outputsize=2"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /batch`

The batch request endpoint allows users to request data for multiple financial instruments, time intervals, and data types simultaneously. This endpoint is useful for efficiently gathering diverse financial data in a single operation, reducing the need for multiple individual requests. Errors in specific requests do not affect the processing of others, and each error is reported separately, enabling easy troubleshooting.

### Request body
Only JSON `POST` requests are supported.
The request content structure consists of key-value items. The key is a unique request ID. The value is requested url.

### Response
The response contains key-value data. The key is a unique request ID. The value is returned data.

### API credits
<ul>
<li>The number of concurrent requests is limited by your subscription plan.</li>
<li>Credits are consumed per requested endpoint, with the total usage equal to the sum of individual requests in the batch.</li>
<li>If the requested data exceeds your available credits, only partial data will be returned asynchronously until your quota is exhausted.</li>
<li>If one or more requests in the batch contain errors (e.g., invalid symbols or unsupported intervals), it will not affect the successful processing of other requests. Errors are reported individually within the response, allowing you to identify and correct specific issues without impacting the entire batch.</li>
</ul>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "property1": {
    "url": "/time_series?symbol=AAPL&interval=1min&apikey=demo&outputsize=2"
  },
  "property2": {
    "url": "/time_series?symbol=AAPL&interval=1min&apikey=demo&outputsize=2"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="batches-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|Map of requests|
|» **additionalProperties**|body|[advanced_request_value](#schemaadvanced_request_value)|false|none|

## Balance sheet

<a id="opIdGetBalanceSheet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.twelvedata.com/balance_sheet \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /balance_sheet`

The balance sheet endpoint provides a detailed financial statement for a company, outlining its assets, liabilities, and shareholders' equity. This endpoint returns structured data that includes current and non-current assets, total liabilities, and equity figures, enabling users to assess a company's financial health and stability.

<h3 id="balance-sheet-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|symbol|query|string|false|Symbol ticker of instrument.<br>For preferred stocks use dot(.) delimiter.<br>E.g. `BRK.A` or `BRK.B` will be correct|
|figi|query|string|false|Filter by financial instrument global identifier (FIGI). This parameter is available on the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing">Ultra</a> plan (individual) and the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing-business">Enterprise</a> plan (business) and above.|
|isin|query|string|false|Filter by international securities identification number (ISIN). ISIN access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|cusip|query|string|false|The CUSIP of an instrument for which data is requested. CUSIP access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|exchange|query|string|false|Exchange where instrument is traded|
|mic_code|query|string|false|Market Identifier Code (MIC) under ISO 10383 standard|
|country|query|string|false|Country where instrument is traded, e.g., `United States` or `US`|
|period|query|[PeriodEnum](#schemaperiodenum)|false|The reporting period for the balance sheet data|
|start_date|query|string|false|Begin date for filtering items by fiscal date.<br>Returns income statements with fiscal dates on or after this date. Format `2006-01-02`|
|end_date|query|string|false|End date for filtering items by fiscal date.<br>Returns income statements with fiscal dates on or before this date. Format `2006-01-02`|
|outputsize|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of records in response|

|period|annual|
|period|quarterly|

|mic_code|query|string|false|Market Identifier Code (MIC) under ISO 10383 standard|

## Cash flow

<a id="opIdGetCashFlow"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.twelvedata.com/cash_flow \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /cash_flow`

The cash flow endpoint provides detailed information on a company's cash flow activities, including the net cash and cash equivalents moving in and out of the business. This data includes operating, investing, and financing cash flows, offering a comprehensive view of the company's liquidity and financial health.

<h3 id="cash-flow-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|symbol|query|string|false|Symbol ticker of instrument.<br>For preferred stocks use dot(.) delimiter.<br>E.g. `BRK.A` or `BRK.B` will be correct|
|figi|query|string|false|Filter by financial instrument global identifier (FIGI). This parameter is available on the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing">Ultra</a> plan (individual) and the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing-business">Enterprise</a> plan (business) and above.|
|isin|query|string|false|Filter by international securities identification number (ISIN). ISIN access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|cusip|query|string|false|The CUSIP of an instrument for which data is requested. CUSIP access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|exchange|query|string|false|Exchange where instrument is traded|
|mic_code|query|string|false|Market Identifier Code (MIC) under ISO 10383 standard|
|country|query|string|false|Country where instrument is traded, e.g., `United States` or `US`|
|period|query|[PeriodEnum](#schemaperiodenum)|false|The reporting period for the cash flow statements|
|start_date|query|string|false|Start date for filtering cash flow statements.<br>Only cash flow statements with fiscal dates on or after this date will be included.<br>Format `2006-01-02`|
|end_date|query|string|false|End date for filtering cash flow statements.<br>Only cash flow statements with fiscal dates on or before this date will be included.<br>Format `2006-01-02`|
|outputsize|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of records in response|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|period|annual|
|period|quarterly|

## Cash flow consolidated

<a id="opIdGetCashFlowConsolidated"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.twelvedata.com/cash_flow/consolidated \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /cash_flow/consolidated`

The cash flow consolidated endpoint provides raw data on a company's consolidated cash flow, including the net cash and cash equivalents moving in and out of the business. It returns information on operating, investing, and financing activities, helping users track liquidity and financial health over a specified period.

<h3 id="cash-flow-consolidated-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|symbol|query|string|false|Symbol ticker of instrument.<br>For preferred stocks use dot(.) delimiter.<br>E.g. `BRK.A` or `BRK.B` will be correct|
|figi|query|string|false|Filter by financial instrument global identifier (FIGI). This parameter is available on the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing">Ultra</a> plan (individual) and the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing-business">Enterprise</a> plan (business) and above.|
|isin|query|string|false|Filter by international securities identification number (ISIN). ISIN access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|cusip|query|string|false|The CUSIP of an instrument for which data is requested. CUSIP access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|exchange|query|string|false|Exchange where instrument is traded|
|mic_code|query|string|false|Market Identifier Code (MIC) under ISO 10383 standard|
|country|query|string|false|Country where instrument is traded, e.g., `United States` or `US`|
|period|query|[PeriodEnum](#schemaperiodenum)|false|The reporting period for the cash flow statements|
|start_date|query|string|false|Start date for filtering cash flow statements. Only cash flow statements with fiscal dates on or after this date will be included.<br>Format `2006-01-02`|
|end_date|query|string|false|End date for filtering cash flow statements. Only cash flow statements with fiscal dates on or before this date will be included.<br>Format `2006-01-02`|
|outputsize|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of records in response|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|period|annual|
|period|quarterly|

## Dividends

<a id="opIdGetDividends"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.twelvedata.com/dividends \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /dividends`

The dividends endpoint provides historical dividend data for a specified stock, in many cases covering over a decade. It returns information on dividend payouts, including the ex-date, amount, and frequency. This endpoint is ideal for users tracking dividend histories or evaluating the income potential of stocks.

<h3 id="dividends-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|symbol|query|string|false|Symbol ticker of instrument. For preferred stocks use dot(.) delimiter.<br>E.g. `BRK.A` or `BRK.B` will be correct|
|figi|query|string|false|Filter by financial instrument global identifier (FIGI). This parameter is available on the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing">Ultra</a> plan (individual) and the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing-business">Enterprise</a> plan (business) and above.|
|isin|query|string|false|Filter by international securities identification number (ISIN). ISIN access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|cusip|query|string|false|The CUSIP of an instrument for which data is requested. CUSIP access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|exchange|query|string|false|Exchange where instrument is traded|
|mic_code|query|string|false|Market Identifier Code (MIC) under ISO 10383 standard|
|country|query|string|false|Country where instrument is traded, e.g., `United States` or `US`|
|range|query|[RangeEnum](#schemarangeenum)|false|Specifies the time range for which to retrieve dividend data.<br>Accepts values such as `last` (most recent dividend), `next` (upcoming dividend),<br>`1m` - `5y` for respective periods, or `full` for all available data.<br>If provided together with `start_date` and/or `end_date`, this parameter takes precedence.|
|start_date|query|string|false|Start date for the dividend data query. Only dividends with dates on or after this date will be returned. Format `2006-01-02`.<br>If provided together with `range` parameter, `range` will take precedence.|
|end_date|query|string|false|End date for the dividend data query. Only dividends with dates on or before this date will be returned. Format `2006-01-02`.<br>If provided together with `range` parameter, `range` will take precedence.|
|adjust|query|boolean|false|Specifies if there should be an adjustment|

## Dividends calendar

<a id="opIdGetDividendsCalendar"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.twelvedata.com/dividends_calendar \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /dividends_calendar`

The dividends calendar endpoint provides a detailed schedule of upcoming and past dividend events for specified date ranges. By using the `start_date` and `end_date` parameters, users can retrieve a list of companies issuing dividends, including the ex-dividend date and dividend amount. This endpoint is ideal for tracking dividend payouts and planning investment strategies based on dividend schedules.

<h3 id="dividends-calendar-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|symbol|query|string|false|Symbol ticker of instrument. For preferred stocks use dot(.) delimiter.<br>E.g. `BRK.A` or `BRK.B` will be correct|
|figi|query|string|false|Filter by financial instrument global identifier (FIGI). This parameter is available on the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing">Ultra</a> plan (individual) and the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing-business">Enterprise</a> plan (business) and above.|
|isin|query|string|false|Filter by international securities identification number (ISIN). ISIN access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|cusip|query|string|false|The CUSIP of an instrument for which data is requested. CUSIP access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|exchange|query|string|false|Exchange where instrument is traded|
|mic_code|query|string|false|Market Identifier Code (MIC) under ISO 10383 standard|
|country|query|string|false|Country where instrument is traded, e.g., `United States` or `US`|
|start_date|query|string|false|Start date for the dividends calendar query. Only dividends with ex-dates on or after this date will be returned. Format `2006-01-02`|
|end_date|query|string|false|End date for the dividends calendar query. Only dividends with ex-dates on or before this date will be returned. Format `2006-01-02`|
|outputsize|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of data points to retrieve.<br>Supports values in the range from `1` to `500`.<br>Default `100` when no date parameters are set, otherwise set to maximum|
|page|query|integer(int64)|false|Page number|

## Earnings

<a id="opIdGetEarnings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.twelvedata.com/earnings \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /earnings`

The earnings endpoint provides comprehensive earnings data for a specified company, including both the estimated and actual Earnings Per Share (EPS) figures. This endpoint delivers historical earnings information, allowing users to track a company's financial performance over time.

<h3 id="earnings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|symbol|query|string|false|Symbol ticker of instrument.<br>For preferred stocks use dot(.) delimiter.<br>E.g. `BRK.A` or `BRK.B` will be correct|
|figi|query|string|false|Filter by financial instrument global identifier (FIGI). This parameter is available on the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing">Ultra</a> plan (individual) and the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing-business">Enterprise</a> plan (business) and above.|
|isin|query|string|false|Filter by international securities identification number (ISIN). ISIN access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|cusip|query|string|false|The CUSIP of an instrument for which data is requested. CUSIP access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|exchange|query|string|false|Exchange where instrument is traded|
|mic_code|query|string|false|Market Identifier Code (MIC) under ISO 10383 standard|
|country|query|string|false|Country where instrument is traded, e.g., `United States` or `US`|
|type|query|[TypeEnum](#schematypeenum)|false|The asset class to which the instrument belongs|
|period|query|[PeriodEarningsEnum](#schemaperiodearningsenum)|false|Type of earning, returns only 1 record.<br>When is not empty, dates and outputsize parameters are ignored|
|outputsize|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of data points to retrieve.<br>Supports values in the range from `1` to `1000`.<br>Default `10` when no date parameters are set, otherwise set to maximum|
|format|query|[FormatEnum](#schemaformatenum)|false|The format of the response data|
|delimiter|query|string|false|The separator used in the CSV response data|
|start_date|query|string|false|The date from which the data is requested. The date format is `YYYY-MM-DD`.|
|end_date|query|string|false|The date to which the data is requested. The date format is `YYYY-MM-DD`.|

`GET /earnings_calendar`

The earnings calendar endpoint provides a schedule of company earnings announcements for a specified date range. By default, it returns earnings data for the current day. Users can customize the date range using the `start_date` and `end_date` parameters to retrieve earnings information for specific periods. This endpoint is useful for tracking upcoming earnings reports and planning around key financial announcements.

<h3 id="earnings-calendar-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|exchange|query|string|false|Exchange where instrument is traded|

|format|query|[FormatEnum](#schemaformatenum)|false|Value can be JSON or CSV|
|delimiter|query|string|false|Specify the delimiter used when downloading the CSV file|
|start_date|query|string|false|Can be used separately and together with end_date.<br>Format `2006-01-02` or `2006-01-02T15:04:05`|
|end_date|query|string|false|Can be used separately and together with start_date.<br>Format `2006-01-02` or `2006-01-02T15:04:05`|
|dp|query|integer(int64)|false|Specifies the number of decimal places for floating values.<br>Should be in range [0,11] inclusive|

`GET /income_statement`

The income statement endpoint provides detailed financial data on a company's income statement, including revenues, expenses, and net income for specified periods, either annually or quarterly. This endpoint is essential for retrieving comprehensive financial performance metrics of a company, allowing users to access historical and current financial results.

<h3 id="income-statement-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|symbol|query|string|false|Symbol ticker of instrument.<br>For preferred stocks use dot(.) delimiter.<br>E.g. `BRK.A` or `BRK.B` will be correct|
|figi|query|string|false|Filter by financial instrument global identifier (FIGI). This parameter is available on the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing">Ultra</a> plan (individual) and the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing-business">Enterprise</a> plan (business) and above.|
|isin|query|string|false|Filter by international securities identification number (ISIN). ISIN access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|cusip|query|string|false|The CUSIP of an instrument for which data is requested. CUSIP access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|exchange|query|string|false|Exchange where instrument is traded|
|mic_code|query|string|false|Market Identifier Code (MIC) under ISO 10383 standard|
|country|query|string|false|Country where instrument is traded, e.g., `United States` or `US`|
|period|query|[PeriodEnum](#schemaperiodenum)|false|The reporting period for the income statement data|
|start_date|query|string|false|Begin date for filtering income statements by fiscal date.<br>Returns income statements with fiscal dates on or after this date.<br>Format `2006-01-02`|
|end_date|query|string|false|End date for filtering income statements by fiscal date.<br>Returns income statements with fiscal dates on or before this date.<br>Format `2006-01-02`|

```json
{
  "meta": {
    "symbol": "AAPL",
```

## Income statement consolidated

<a id="opIdGetIncomeStatementConsolidated"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.twelvedata.com/income_statement/consolidated \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /income_statement/consolidated`

The income statement consolidated endpoint provides a company's raw income statement, detailing revenue, expenses, and net income for specified periods, either annually or quarterly. This data is essential for evaluating a company's financial performance over time, allowing users to access comprehensive financial results in a structured format.

<h3 id="income-statement-consolidated-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|symbol|query|string|false|Symbol ticker of instrument.<br>For preferred stocks use dot(.) delimiter.<br>E.g. `BRK.A` or `BRK.B` will be correct|
|figi|query|string|false|Filter by financial instrument global identifier (FIGI). This parameter is available on the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing">Ultra</a> plan (individual) and the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing-business">Enterprise</a> plan (business) and above.|
|isin|query|string|false|Filter by international securities identification number (ISIN). ISIN access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|cusip|query|string|false|The CUSIP of an instrument for which data is requested. CUSIP access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|exchange|query|string|false|Exchange where instrument is traded|
|mic_code|query|string|false|Market Identifier Code (MIC) under ISO 10383 standard|
|country|query|string|false|Country where instrument is traded, e.g., `United States` or `US`|
|period|query|[PeriodEnum](#schemaperiodenum)|false|The reporting period for the income statement data|
|start_date|query|string|false|Begin date for filtering income statements by fiscal date.<br>Returns income statements with fiscal dates on or after this date.<br>Format `2006-01-02`|
|end_date|query|string|false|End date for filtering income statements by fiscal date.<br>Returns income statements with fiscal dates on or before this date.<br>Format `2006-01-02`|
|outputsize|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of records in response|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|period|annual|
|period|quarterly|

## IPO calendar

<a id="opIdGetIpoCalendar"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.twelvedata.com/ipo_calendar \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /ipo_calendar`

The IPO Calendar endpoint provides detailed information on initial public offerings (IPOs), including those that have occurred in the past, are happening today, or are scheduled for the future. Users can access data such as company names, IPO dates, and offering details, allowing them to track and monitor IPO activity efficiently.

<h3 id="ipo-calendar-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|exchange|query|string|false|Exchange where instrument is traded|
|mic_code|query|string|false|Market Identifier Code (MIC) under ISO 10383 standard|
|country|query|string|false|Country where instrument is traded, e.g., `United States` or `US`|
|start_date|query|string|false|The earliest IPO date to include in the results. Format: `2006-01-02`|
|end_date|query|string|false|The latest IPO date to include in the results. Format: `2006-01-02`|

## Last changes

<a id="opIdGetLastChanges"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.twelvedata.com/last_change/statistics \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /last_change/{endpoint}`

The last change endpoint provides the most recent updates to fundamental data for a specified dataset. It returns a timestamp indicating when the data was last modified, allowing users to efficiently manage API requests by only fetching new data when changes occur. This helps optimize data retrieval and reduce unnecessary API credit usage.

<h3 id="last-changes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|endpoint|path|[EndpointEnum](#schemaendpointenum)|true|Endpoint name|
|start_date|query|string|false|The starting date and time for data selection, in `2006-01-02T15:04:05` format|
|symbol|query|string|false|Filter by symbol|
|exchange|query|string|false|Filter by exchange name|
|mic_code|query|string|false|Filter by market identifier code (MIC) under ISO 10383 standard|
|country|query|string|false|Filter by country name or alpha code, e.g., `United States` or `US`|
|page|query|integer(int64)|false|Page number|
|outputsize|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of records in response|

<a id="opIdPressReleasesListParameters"></a>


`GET /press_releases`

The press releases endpoint offers structured, real-time access to official company press releases and corporate announcements from public entities across global markets.

<h3 id="press-releases-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|symbol|query|string|false|Symbol ticker of instrument.<br>For preferred stocks use dot(.) delimiter.<br>E.g. `BRK.A` or `BRK.B` will be correct|
|figi|query|string|false|Filter by financial instrument global identifier (FIGI). This parameter is available on the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing">Ultra</a> plan (individual) and the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing-business">Enterprise</a> plan (business) and above.|
|isin|query|string|false|Filter by international securities identification number (ISIN). ISIN access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|cusip|query|string|false|The CUSIP of an instrument for which data is requested. CUSIP access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|exchange|query|string|false|Exchange where instrument is traded|
|mic_code|query|string|false|Market Identifier Code (MIC) under ISO 10383 standard|
|start_date|query|string|false|Begin date for filtering items.<br>Returns press releases with release date on or after this date. Format `2025-12-24T02:07:00`|
|end_date|query|string|false|End date for filtering items.<br>Returns press releases with release date on or before this date. Format `2025-12-24T02:07:00`|
|timezone|query|string|false|Time zone for date filtering. Default is the identifier time zone.|
|language|query|string|false|Comma-separated list of languages to filter press releases by language.|
|outputsize|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of press releases returned per page. Default is `2`, maximum is `10`.<br><br>type: number|
|page|query|integer(int64)|false|Page number to return, starting at `1`. Use it together with `outputsize` to walk the result set.<br><br>type: number|

## Splits calendar

<a id="opIdGetSplitsCalendar"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.twelvedata.com/splits_calendar \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /splits_calendar`

The splits calendar endpoint provides a detailed calendar of stock split events within a specified date range. By setting the `start_date` and `end_date` parameters, users can retrieve a list of upcoming or past stock splits, including the company name, split ratio, and effective date. This endpoint is useful for tracking changes in stock structure and planning investment strategies around these events.

<h3 id="splits-calendar-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|symbol|query|string|false|Symbol ticker of instrument. For preferred stocks use dot(.) delimiter.<br>E.g. `BRK.A` or `BRK.B` will be correct|
|figi|query|string|false|Filter by financial instrument global identifier (FIGI). This parameter is available on the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing">Ultra</a> plan (individual) and the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing-business">Enterprise</a> plan (business) and above.|
|isin|query|string|false|Filter by international securities identification number (ISIN). ISIN access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|cusip|query|string|false|The CUSIP of an instrument for which data is requested. CUSIP access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|exchange|query|string|false|Exchange where instrument is traded|
|mic_code|query|string|false|Market Identifier Code (MIC) under ISO 10383 standard|
|country|query|string|false|Country where instrument is traded, e.g., `United States` or `US`|
|start_date|query|string|false|The starting date (inclusive) for filtering split events in the calendar. Format `2006-01-02`|
|end_date|query|string|false|The ending date (inclusive) for filtering split events in the calendar. Format `2006-01-02`|
|outputsize|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of data points to retrieve. Supports values in the range from `1` to `500`. Default `100` when no date parameters are set, otherwise set to maximum|
|page|query|string|false|Page number|

## Statistics

<a id="opIdGetStatistics"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.twelvedata.com/statistics \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /statistics`

The statistics endpoint provides a comprehensive snapshot of a company's key financial statistics, including valuation metrics, revenue figures, profit margins, and other essential financial data. This endpoint is ideal for users seeking detailed insights into a company's financial health and performance metrics.

|isin|query|string|false|Filter by international securities identification number (ISIN). ISIN access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|cusip|query|string|false|The CUSIP of an instrument for which data is requested. CUSIP access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|exchange|query|string|false|Exchange where instrument is traded|
|mic_code|query|string|false|Market Identifier Code (MIC) under ISO 10383 standard|
|country|query|string|false|Country where instrument is traded, e.g., `United States` or `US`|

## Fixed income

<a id="opIdGetBonds"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.twelvedata.com/bonds \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /bonds`

The fixed income endpoint provides a daily updated list of available bonds. It returns an array containing detailed information about each bond, including identifiers, names, and other relevant attributes.

<h3 id="fixed-income-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|symbol|query|string|false|The ticker symbol of an instrument for which data is requested|

|mic_code|query|string|false|Filter by market identifier code (MIC) under ISO 10383 standard|
|country|query|string|false|Filter by country name or alpha code, e.g., `United States` or `US`|
|format|query|[FormatEnum](#schemaformatenum)|false|The format of the response data|
|delimiter|query|string|false|The separator used in the CSV response data|
|show_plan|query|boolean|false|Adds info on which plan symbol is available|
|page|query|integer(int64)|false|Page number of the results to fetch|
|outputsize|query|integer(int64)|false|Determines the number of data points returned in the output. If not specified, all available records are returned|

## Cross listings

<a id="opIdGetCrossListings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.twelvedata.com/cross_listings?symbol=AAPL' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /cross_listings`

The cross_listings endpoint provides a daily updated list of cross-listed symbols for a specified financial instrument. Cross-listed symbols represent the same security available on multiple exchanges. This endpoint is useful for identifying all the exchanges where a particular security is traded, allowing users to access comprehensive trading information across different markets.

<h3 id="cross-listings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|symbol|query|string|true|The ticker symbol of an instrument for which data is requested|
|exchange|query|string|false|Exchange where instrument is traded|
|mic_code|query|string|false|Market identifier code (MIC) under ISO 10383 standard|
|country|query|string|false|Country to which stock exchange belongs to|

## Earliest timestamp

<a id="opIdGetEarliestTimestamp"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.twelvedata.com/earliest_timestamp?interval=1day' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /earliest_timestamp`

The earliest_timestamp endpoint provides the earliest available date and time for a specified financial instrument at a given data interval. This endpoint is useful for determining the starting point of historical data availability for various assets, such as stocks or currencies, allowing users to understand the time range covered by the data.

<h3 id="earliest-timestamp-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|symbol|query|string|false|Symbol ticker of the instrument.|
|figi|query|string|false|Filter by financial instrument global identifier (FIGI). This parameter is available on the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing">Ultra</a> plan (individual) and the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing-business">Enterprise</a> plan (business) and above.|
|isin|query|string|false|Filter by international securities identification number (ISIN). ISIN access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|cusip|query|string|false|The CUSIP of an instrument for which data is requested. CUSIP access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|interval|query|[IntervalEnum](#schemaintervalenum)|true|Interval between two consecutive points in time series.|
|exchange|query|string|false|Exchange where instrument is traded.|
|mic_code|query|string|false|Market Identifier Code (MIC) under ISO 10383 standard.|
|timezone|query|string|false|Timezone at which output datetime will be displayed. Supports:<br><ul><br><li>1. <code>Exchange</code> for local exchange time</li><br><li>2. <code>UTC</code> for datetime at universal UTC standard</li><br><li>3. Timezone name according to the IANA Time Zone Database. E.g. <code>America/New_York</code>, <code>Asia/Singapore</code>. Full list of timezones can be found <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tz_database_time_zones" target="blank">here</a>.</li><br></ul><br><p>Interval Limitation: The timezone parameter is only applicable for intraday intervals (less than 1 day). For intervals of 1day, 1week, or 1month, the timezone parameter is ignored, and data is strictly returned in the Exchange local time.</p><br><i>Take note that the IANA Timezone name is case-sensitive</i>|

#### Enumerated Values

|interval|5min|
|interval|15min|
|interval|30min|
|interval|45min|
|interval|1h|
|interval|2h|
|interval|4h|
|interval|8h|
|interval|1day|
|interval|1week|
|interval|1month|

## Exchanges schedule

<a id="opIdGetExchangeSchedule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.twelvedata.com/exchange_schedule \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /exchange_schedule`

The exchanges schedule endpoint provides detailed information about various stock exchanges, including their trading hours and operational days. This data is essential for users who need to know when specific exchanges are open for trading, allowing them to plan their activities around the availability of these markets.

<h3 id="exchanges-schedule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|mic_name|query|string|false|Filter by exchange name|
|mic_code|query|string|false|Filter by market identifier code (MIC) under ISO 10383 standard|
|country|query|string|false|Filter by country name or alpha code, e.g., `United States` or `US`|
|date|query|string|false|<p><br>If a date is provided, the API returns the schedule for the specified date; otherwise, it returns the default (common) schedule.<br></p><br>The date can be specified in one of the following formats:<br><ul><br><li>An exact date (e.g., <code>2021-10-27</code>)</li><br><li>A human-readable keyword: <code>today</code> or <code>yesterday</code></li><br><li>A full datetime string in UTC (e.g., <code>2025-04-11T20:00:00</code>) to retrieve the schedule corresponding to the day in the specified time.</li><br></ul><br>When using a datetime value, the resulting schedule will correspond to the local calendar day at the specified time.<br>For example, <code>2025-04-11T20:00:00 UTC</code> corresponds to:<br><ul><br><li><code>2025-04-11</code> in the <code>America/New_York</code> timezone</li><br><li><code>2025-04-12</code> in the <code>Australia/Sydney</code> timezone</li><br></ul>|

```bash
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /symbol_search`

The symbol search endpoint allows users to find financial instruments by name or symbol. It returns a list of matching symbols, ordered by relevance, with the most relevant instrument first. This is useful for quickly locating specific stocks, ETFs, or other financial instruments when only partial information is available.

<h3 id="symbol-search-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|symbol|query|string|true|Symbol to search. Supports:<br><ul><br><li>Ticker symbol of instrument.</li><br><li>International securities identification number (ISIN). ISIN access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section</li><br><li>The FIGI (Financial Instrument Global Identifier) parameter is available on the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing">Ultra</a> plan (individual) and <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing-business">Enterprise</a> plan (business) and above.</li><br><li>Composite FIGI parameter is available on the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing">Ultra</a> plan (individual) and <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing-business">Enterprise</a> plan (business) and above.</li><br><li>Share Class FIGI parameter is available on the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing">Ultra</a> plan (individual) and <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing-business">Enterprise</a> plan (business) and above.</li><br></ul>|
|outputsize|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of matches in response. Max <code>120</code>|
|show_plan|query|boolean|false|Adds info on which plan symbol is available.|

## Currency conversion

<a id="opIdGetCurrencyConversion"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.twelvedata.com/currency_conversion?symbol=EUR%2FUSD&amount=100' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /currency_conversion`

The currency conversion endpoint provides real-time exchange rates and calculates the converted amount for specified currency pairs, including both forex and cryptocurrencies. This endpoint is useful for obtaining up-to-date conversion values between two currencies, facilitating tasks such as financial reporting, e-commerce transactions, and travel budgeting.

<h3 id="currency-conversion-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|symbol|query|string|true|The currency pair you want to request can be either forex or cryptocurrency. Slash(`/`) delimiter is used. E.g. `EUR/USD` or `BTC/ETH` will be correct|
|amount|query|number(double)|true|Amount of base currency to be converted into quote currency. Supports values in the range from `0` and above|
|date|query|string|false|If not null, will use exchange rate from a specific date or time. Format `2006-01-02` or `2006-01-02T15:04:05`. Is set in the local exchange time zone, use timezone parameter to specify a specific time zone|
|format|query|[FormatEnum](#schemaformatenum)|false|Value can be `JSON` or `CSV`. Default `JSON`|
|delimiter|query|string|false|Specify the delimiter used when downloading the `CSV` file. Default semicolon `;`|
|dp|query|integer(int64)|false|The number of decimal places for the data|
|timezone|query|string|false|Timezone at which output datetime will be displayed. Supports:<br><ul><br><li>1. <code>Exchange</code> for local exchange time</li><br><li>2. <code>UTC</code> for datetime at universal UTC standard</li><br><li>3. Timezone name according to the IANA Time Zone Database. E.g. <code>America/New_York</code>, <code>Asia/Singapore</code>. Full list of timezones can be found <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tz_database_time_zones" target="blank">here</a>.</li><br></ul><br><i>Take note that the IANA Timezone name is case-sensitive</i>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|format|JSON|
|format|CSV|

## Direct holders

<a id="opIdGetDirectHolders"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.twelvedata.com/direct_holders \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /direct_holders`

The direct holders endpoint provides detailed information about the number of shares directly held by individuals or entities as recorded in a company's official share registry. This data is essential for understanding the distribution of stock ownership within a company, helping users identify major shareholders and assess shareholder concentration.

<h3 id="direct-holders-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|symbol|query|string|false|Symbol ticker of instrument.<br>For preferred stocks use dot(.) delimiter.<br>E.g. `BRK.A` or `BRK.B` will be correct|
|figi|query|string|false|Filter by financial instrument global identifier (FIGI). This parameter is available on the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing">Ultra</a> plan (individual) and the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing-business">Enterprise</a> plan (business) and above.|
|isin|query|string|false|Filter by international securities identification number (ISIN). ISIN access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|cusip|query|string|false|The CUSIP of an instrument for which data is requested. CUSIP access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|exchange|query|string|false|Exchange where instrument is traded|
|mic_code|query|string|false|Market Identifier Code (MIC) under ISO 10383 standard|
|country|query|string|false|Country where instrument is traded, e.g., `United States` or `US`|

## EDGAR fillings

<a id="opIdGetEdgarFilingsArchive"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.twelvedata.com/edgar_filings/archive \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /edgar_filings/archive`

The EDGAR fillings endpoint provides access to a comprehensive collection of financial documents submitted to the SEC, including real-time and historical forms, filings, and exhibits. Users can retrieve detailed information about company disclosures, financial statements, and regulatory submissions, enabling them to access essential compliance and financial data directly from the SEC's EDGAR system.

<h3 id="edgar-fillings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|symbol|query|string|false|The ticker symbol of an instrument for which data is requested|
|figi|query|string|false|Filter by financial instrument global identifier (FIGI). This parameter is available on the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing">Ultra</a> plan (individual) and the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing-business">Enterprise</a> plan (business) and above.|
|isin|query|string|false|Filter by international securities identification number (ISIN). ISIN access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|cusip|query|string|false|The CUSIP of an instrument for which data is requested. CUSIP access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|exchange|query|string|false|Filter by exchange name|
|mic_code|query|string|false|Filter by market identifier code (MIC) under ISO 10383 standard|
|country|query|string|false|Filter by country name or alpha code, e.g., `United States` or `US`|
|form_type|query|string|false|Filter by form types, example `8-K`, `EX-1.1`|
|filled_from|query|string|false|Filter by filled date from|
|filled_to|query|string|false|Filter by filled date to|
|page|query|integer(int64)|false|Page number|
|page_size|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of records in response|

> Code samples

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /eod`

The End of Day (EOD) Prices endpoint provides the closing price and other relevant metadata for a financial instrument at the end of a trading day. This endpoint is useful for retrieving daily historical data for stocks, ETFs, or other securities, allowing users to track performance over time and compare daily market movements.

<h3 id="end-of-day-price-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|symbol|query|string|false|Symbol ticker of the instrument|
|figi|query|string|false|Filter by financial instrument global identifier (FIGI). This parameter is available on the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing">Ultra</a> plan (individual) and the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing-business">Enterprise</a> plan (business) and above.|
|isin|query|string|false|Filter by international securities identification number (ISIN). ISIN access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|cusip|query|string|false|The CUSIP of an instrument for which data is requested. CUSIP access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|exchange|query|string|false|Exchange where instrument is traded|
|mic_code|query|string|false|Market Identifier Code (MIC) under ISO 10383 standard|
|country|query|string|false|Country where instrument is traded, e.g., `United States` or `US`|
|type|query|[TypeEnum](#schematypeenum)|false|The asset class to which the instrument belongs|
|date|query|string|false|If not null, then return data from a specific date|
|prepost|query|boolean|false|Parameter is optional. Only for the `Pro` plan (individual) and `Venture` plan (business) and above.<br>Available at the `1min`, `5min`, `15min`, and `30min` intervals for US equities.<br>Open, high, low, close values are supplied without volume|
|dp|query|integer(int64)|false|Specifies the number of decimal places for floating values<br>Should be in range [0,11] inclusive|

|type|American Depositary Receipt|
|type|Bond|
|type|Bond Fund|
|type|Closed-end Fund|
|type|Common Stock|
|type|Depositary Receipt|
|type|Digital Currency|
|type|ETF|
|type|Exchange-Traded Note|
|type|Global Depositary Receipt|
|type|Limited Partnership|
|type|Mutual Fund|
|type|Physical Currency|

## Market movers

<a id="opIdGetMarketMovers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.twelvedata.com/market_movers/stocks \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /market_movers/{market}`

The market movers endpoint provides a ranked list of the top-gaining and losing assets for the current trading day. It returns detailed data on the highest percentage price increases and decreases since the previous day's close. This endpoint supports international equities, forex, and cryptocurrencies, enabling users to quickly identify significant market movements across various asset classes.

<h3 id="market-movers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|market|path|[MarketEnum](#schemamarketenum)|true|Market type|
|direction|query|[DirectionEnum](#schemadirectionenum)|false|Specifies direction of the snapshot gainers or losers|
|outputsize|query|integer(int64)|false|Specifies the size of the snapshot.<br>Can be in a range from `1` to `50`|
|country|query|string|false|Country of the snapshot, applicable to non-currencies only.<br>Takes country name or alpha code|
|price_greater_than|query|string|false|Takes values with price grater than specified value|
|dp|query|string|false|Specifies the number of decimal places for floating values.<br>Should be in range [0,11] inclusive|

|---|---|
|market|stocks|
|market|etf|

|direction|losers|

## Quote

<a id="opIdGetQuote"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.twelvedata.com/quote \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /quote`

The quote endpoint provides real-time data for a selected financial instrument, returning essential information such as the latest price, open, high, low, close, volume, and price change. This endpoint is ideal for users needing up-to-date market data to track price movements and trading activity for specific stocks, ETFs, or other securities.

<h3 id="quote-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|symbol|query|string|false|Symbol ticker of the instrument|
|figi|query|string|false|Filter by financial instrument global identifier (FIGI). This parameter is available on the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing">Ultra</a> plan (individual) and the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing-business">Enterprise</a> plan (business) and above.|
|isin|query|string|false|Filter by international securities identification number (ISIN). ISIN access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|cusip|query|string|false|The CUSIP of an instrument for which data is requested. CUSIP access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|interval|query|[IntervalEnum](#schemaintervalenum)|false|Interval of the quote|
|exchange|query|string|false|Exchange where instrument is traded|
|mic_code|query|string|false|Market Identifier Code (MIC) under ISO 10383 standard|
|country|query|string|false|Country where instrument is traded, e.g., `United States` or `US`|
|volume_time_period|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of periods for Average Volume|
|type|query|[TypeEnum](#schematypeenum)|false|The asset class to which the instrument belongs|
|format|query|[FormatEnum](#schemaformatenum)|false|Value can be JSON or CSV<br>Default JSON|
|delimiter|query|string|false|Specify the delimiter used when downloading the CSV file|
|prepost|query|boolean|false|Parameter is optional. Only for the `Pro` plan (individual) and `Venture` plan (business) and above.<br>Available at the `1min`, `5min`, `15min`, and `30min` intervals for US equities.<br>Open, high, low, close values are supplied without volume.|
|eod|query|boolean|false|If true, then return data for closed day|
|rolling_period|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of hours for calculate rolling change at period. By default set to 24, it can be in range [1, 168].|
|dp|query|integer(int64)|false|Specifies the number of decimal places for floating values<br>Should be in range [0,11] inclusive|
|timezone|query|string|false|Timezone at which output datetime will be displayed. Supports:<br><ul><br><li>1. <code>Exchange</code> for local exchange time</li><br><li>2. <code>UTC</code> for datetime at universal UTC standard</li><br><li>3. Timezone name according to the IANA Time Zone Database. E.g. <code>America/New_York</code>, <code>Asia/Singapore</code>. Full list of timezones can be found <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tz_database_time_zones" target="blank">here</a>.</li><br></ul><br><p>Interval Limitation: The timezone parameter is only applicable for intraday intervals (less than 1 day). For intervals of 1day, 1week, or 1month, the timezone parameter is ignored, and data is strictly returned in the Exchange local time.</p><br><i>Take note that the IANA Timezone name is case-sensitive</i>|

## Time series

<a id="opIdGetTimeSeries"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.twelvedata.com/time_series?interval=1min' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /time_series`

The time series endpoint provides detailed historical data for a specified financial instrument. It returns two main components: metadata, which includes essential information about the instrument, and a time series dataset. The time series consists of chronological entries with Open, High, Low, and Close prices, and for applicable instruments, it also includes trading volume. This endpoint is ideal for retrieving comprehensive historical price data for analysis or visualization purposes.

<h3 id="time-series-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|symbol|query|string|false|Symbol ticker of the instrument. E.g. `AAPL`, `EUR/USD`, `ETH/BTC`, ...|
|isin|query|string|false|Filter by international securities identification number (ISIN). ISIN access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|figi|query|string|false|The FIGI of an instrument for which data is requested. This parameter is available on the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing">Ultra</a> plan (individual) and the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/pricing-business">Enterprise</a> plan (business) and above.|
|cusip|query|string|false|The CUSIP of an instrument for which data is requested. CUSIP access is activating in the <a href="https://twelvedata.com/account/add-ons">Data add-ons</a> section|
|interval|query|[IntervalEnum](#schemaintervalenum)|true|Interval between two consecutive points in time series|
|outputsize|query|integer(int64)|false|Number of data points to retrieve. Supports values in the range from `1` to `5000`. Default `30` when no date parameters are set, otherwise set to maximum|
|exchange|query|string|false|Exchange where instrument is traded|
|mic_code|query|string|false|Market Identifier Code (MIC) under ISO 10383 standard|
|country|query|string|false|The country where the instrument is traded, e.g., `United States` or `US`|
|type|query|[TypeEnum](#schematypeenum)|false|The asset class to which the instrument belongs|
|timezone|query|string|false|Timezone at which output datetime will be displayed. Supports:<br><ul><br><li>1. <code>Exchange</code> for local exchange time</li><br><li>2. <code>UTC</code> for datetime at universal UTC standard</li><br><li>3. Timezone name according to the IANA Time Zone Database. E.g. <code>America/New_York</code>, <code>Asia/Singapore</code>. Full list of timezones can be found <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tz_database_time_zones" target="blank">here</a></li><br></ul><br><p>Interval Limitation: The timezone parameter is only applicable for intraday intervals (less than 1 day). For intervals of 1day, 1week, or 1month, the timezone parameter is ignored, and data is strictly returned in the Exchange local time.</p><br><i>Take note that the IANA Timezone name is case-sensitive</i>|
|start_date|query|string|false|Can be used separately and together with `end_date`. Format `2006-01-02` or `2006-01-02T15:04:05`<br><br>Default location:<br><ul><br><li>Forex and Cryptocurrencies - <code>UTC</code></li><br><li>Stocks - where exchange is located (e.g. for AAPL it will be <code>America/New_York</code>)</li><br></ul><br>Both parameters take into account if <code>timezone</code> parameter is provided.<br/><br>If <code>timezone</code> is given then, <code>start_date</code> and <code>end_date</code> will be used in the specified location<br><br>Examples:<br><ul><br><li>1. <code>&symbol=AAPL&start_date=2019-08-09T15:50:00&…</code><br/><br>Returns all records starting from 2019-08-09T15:50:00 New York time up to current date</li><br><li>2. <code>&symbol=EUR/USD&timezone=Asia/Singapore&start_date=2019-08-09T15:50:00&…</code><br/><br>Returns all records starting from 2019-08-09T15:50:00 Singapore time up to current date</li><br><li>3. <code>&symbol=ETH/BTC&timezone=Europe/Zurich&start_date=2019-08-09T15:50:00&end_date=2019-08-09T15:55:00&...</code><br/><br>Returns all records starting from 2019-08-09T15:50:00 Zurich time up to 2019-08-09T15:55:00</li><br></ul>|
|end_date|query|string|false|The ending date and time for data selection, see `start_date` description for details.|
|date|query|string|false|Specifies the exact date to get the data for. Could be the exact date, e.g. `2021-10-27`, or in human language `today` or `yesterday`|
|order|query|[OrderEnum](#schemaorderenum)|false|Sorting order of the output|
|prepost|query|boolean|false|Returns quotes that include pre-market and post-market data. Only for the `Pro` plan (individual) and `Venture` plan (business) and above.<br>Available at the `1min`, `5min`, `15min`, and `30min` intervals for US equities.<br>Open, high, low, close values are supplied without volume|
|format|query|[FormatEnum](#schemaformatenum)|false|The format of the response data|
|delimiter|query|string|false|The separator used in the CSV response data|
|dp|query|integer(int64)|false|Specifies the number of decimal places for floating values.<br>Should be in range [0, 11] inclusive.<br>By default, the number of decimal places is automatically determined based on the values provided|
|previous_close|query|boolean|false|A boolean parameter to include the previous closing price in the time_series data. If true, adds previous bar close price value to the current object|
|adjust|query|[AdjustEnum](#schemaadjustenum)|false|Adjusting mode for prices|
